name: Add Points
description: There are n points on a straight line, and the i -th point among them is located at x i . All these coordinates are distinct. Determine the number m — the smallest number of points you should add on the line to make the distances between all neighboring points equal.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer n ( 3 ≤ n ≤ 100 000 ) — the number of points. The second line contains a sequence of integers x 1 , x 2 , ..., x n ( - 10 9 ≤ x i ≤ 10 9 ) — the coordinates of the points. All these coordinates are distinct. The points can be given in an arbitrary order.
output_specification: Print a single integer m — the smallest number of points you should add on the line to make the distances between all neighboring points equal.
approach_summary: Precompute linear sieve to store minimum prime factor (spf[x]) up to N in O(N). Factorize any number x ≤ N in O(log x) steps.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 926B — Add Points [242. Sieve, Prime Factorization and Divisors]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Every composite integer $X$ has at least one prime factor $\le \sqrt{X}$. Precomputing the Smallest Prime Factor (SPF) for all numbers up to $M$ via a linear sieve allows any $X \le M$ to be completely prime-factorized in $O(\log X)$ steps.
